review_candidates.title: Engineering Manager (Acquired Products & VPN) (Remote)
review_candidates.description: Who We Are (Mode.Inc) Mode.Inc is the parent company of a portfolio of technology businesses, including Mode Mobile, the creator of EarnOS, a transformational software platform that turns ordinary smartphones into "EarnPhones". This innovation empowers users worldwide to monetize everyday mobile activities such as streaming, gaming, and shopping. We enable users to profit from their data and attention, rather than letting only tech giants benefit. What sets us apart is our inclusive approach, converting users into earners, facilitating over $150M in earnings and savings, and going a step further by turning earners into owners by awarding stock ownership in Mode.Inc based on their usage. We have attracted over 40 million users across 170 countries. Mode Mobile, Inc. Ranked Number 1 Fastest Growing Company in North America on the 2023 Deloitte Technology Fast 500. For additional insights, check out information about our reward-based super app, Mode Earn App, which also powers the reward engine for our proprietary smartphone, Mode Earn Phone. Our Team and Culture Drive Our Success Our team is the heart of our culture. We value innovation, collaboration, and curiosity, with a passion for getting things done. We strive to hire and cultivate the best team members and foster a culture of open communication and transparency. We are driven and hard-working but also committed to having fun along the way. We allow OKRs to guide us, assume positive intent, sometimes agree to disagree and commit, honor our commitments, seek to accomplish more with less, and encourage everyone to speak up as our team owns our company's success. You can read more about our team and how we work here. The Role Mode Mobile is looking for a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead the engineering team taking ownership of a VPN product following its acquisition, and to become a technical leader for future acquired products. This role sits at the intersection of engineering leadership, product ownership, and technical acquisition integration. You will take unfamiliar, live products from acquisition through transition, stabilization, integration, and ongoing growth. We are a user-facing product-led team, and we are looking for someone who is passionate about turning acquired products into thriving, well-run businesses. This is a player-coach role. Initially you will be hands-on with development and operations alongside your engineers: reviewing and writing code, closing knowledge gaps left by the previous team, and making the architectural and prioritization calls that come with inheriting a live product. As the team grows and the transition stabilizes, your focus will shift toward people leadership, delivery management, and building a repeatable playbook for onboarding future acquisitions. You'll work closely with the VP of Engineering, Product Managers, other Engineering Managers, Corporate development, Marketing, Operations, and several stakeholders to define and execute according to our strategic roadmap to accelerate our future growth. Who You Are and What You'll Do You are passionate about giving people private, secure, and unrestricted access to the internet, and about helping users get more value from their smartphones. You care about your users and your team in equal measure. You are a strong engineer who chose to lead: you can still read a Kotlin, Swift, or Go pull request critically, debug a production incident, and make sound architecture decisions, and you enjoy stepping in when the team needs it. Acquisition and Integration Lead technical onboarding of acquired products from due diligence through transition and steady-state ownership. Assess inherited architecture, infrastructure, security, vendors, operational risks, and technical debt. Establish knowledge transfer and ensure critical operational knowledge is documented. Define and execute the transition plan with the acquired team and Mode stakeholders. Build and continuously improve a repeatable engineering acquisition playbook. You are comfortable operating with incomplete information. Acquired products rarely come with perfect documentation, clean architecture, or complete ownership records. You know how to establish the facts quickly, identify the highest risks, and make pragmatic decisions without waiting for perfect information. You build teams: you hire, onboard, coach, and grow engineers, run effective 1:1s, give candid feedback, and create a culture of ownership, testing, and continuous delivery. You embrace agentic AI as a force multiplier for your team: you use AI coding agents yourself for code, investigation, and documentation, and you set the standards and workflows for how your engineers use them safely and productively. You value working closely with Product Management, learning directly from users about what matters to them, and developing solutions that they love. You run delivery well: 2-week sprints, clear OKRs, sensible estimation, and honest status reporting up to leadership, with a bias toward finding minimal ways to test hypotheses and validate feasibility. You're a strong advocate for unit/integration testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and continuously shipping to production, and you will establish them where they don't exist yet. You are security- and compliance-minded: secrets management, encryption, key handling, user privacy, and regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, and SOC 2 are part of how you run a team that operates a privacy product. What You Bring to the Team Must Have: 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 2+ years managing engineers as a people manager or hands-on tech lead/manager in an agile environment delivering consumer products to end-users. Strong hands-on technical background, with deep expertise in at least one of our core areas and enough breadth to work effectively across the stack. Experience in two or more of the following is a strong plus: Native mobile: Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) and/or iOS (Swift, UIKit/SwiftUI), including app store release management Backend services in Go (preferred), Python, or Node.js, with PostgreSQL and AWS (Lambda, S3, RDS) Infrastructure and DevOps: Terraform, Ansible, Docker, multi-cloud/multi-provider hosting, Datadog or similar observability Networking and VPN fundamentals: WireGuard, Shadowsocks or similar, DNS, TLS, and how mobile VPN clients and servers fit together Experience leading or being a key contributor in a technical acquisition, migration, or takeover of a live product: due diligence, transition planning, knowledge transfer, and integration into a parent organization. A track record of raising engineering quality on an inherited system: introducing automated testing, CI/CD, code review, documentation, and security hardening without stopping feature delivery. Agentic AI proficiency: Strong practical experience using AI coding agents and other AI tools for software development, investigation, testing, and documentation, with an understanding of how to use them safely and effectively within an engineering team. You're a candid and empathetic communicator that is excited to join a startup that enjoys leveling up a company, and you are comfortable communicating status, risks, and trade-offs to executives. You have exceptional organizational and analytical skills leading to confident independent delivery, but know when and how to include others. You have experience building and operating large-scale systems and have led technical direction for a team. Passionate about Technology and keeping up to date with latest advancements, techniques and best practices. Alignment with our Core Values: Accountable: You take ownership of your responsibilities, demonstrating trustworthiness and self-discipline. You are consistent in your work, transparent in your actions, and communicate effectively. You follow through on commitments and strive for continuous improvement. Action-driven: Identify what is most important, agree on scope, timely execute, and drive the greatest impact. You take initiative, roll up your sleeves, and get things done. Caring: You genuinely care about yourself and others, our business and craft, our mission and vision, and are passionate in heart and mind. You understand the importance of our team and strive to create a positive, supportive work environment. Curious: You focus on the 'why,' learn and expand your knowledge, explore new ideas, and generally make things better. You're a lifelong learner with a thirst for knowledge and a constant desire to improve. Thorough: Your work is thoughtful, impactful, timely, accurate, and complete. You pay attention to detail, are meticulous, and ensure quality work and compliance. Nice to Have: Experience running a consumer VPN, proxy, or privacy product, including operating in restrictive network environments and handling law-enforcement / data requests Experience managing distributed, remote, multi-timezone teams, including contractors or a small inherited team Experience with subscription businesses: in-app purchases, Stripe, RevenueCat, attribution and analytics (Mixpanel, Amplitude, Firebase) Experience with vendor and cost management across multiple cloud and hosting providers Compliance program experience (SOC 2, GDPR, CCPA) and security audits Experience building an acquisition-integration playbook or an internal engineering standards program. What Success Looks Like In your first 90 days: You understand the recently acquired VPN product architecture, infrastructure, product, operational dependencies and business context. Critical technical and security risks are identified and prioritized. Knowledge gaps from the acquisition are closed. The team has clear ownership, delivery cadence, and operational responsibilities. Within 6 months: App is operating reliably within Mode's engineering standards. The team is shipping predictably and improving the product. Key technical debt and infrastructure risks are under control. You have established a repeatable approach to evaluating and onboarding future acquisitions. Longer term: You build a strong engineering team capable of owning acquired products independently. You lead technical integration of additional acquisitions. You continuously improve Mode's acquisition-to-operation playbook. We Believe in the Following Workplace Norms Allow OKRs to Guide Us Assume Positive Intent Agree to Disagree & Commit Set New Precedents Accomplish More with Less Hold Yourself & Others to High Standards Speak Up Be Resourceful Follow the 80/20 Rule What We Are Offering We are a 100% remote-first, global company. A competitive compensation package. We offer generous perks and benefits to team members. Participation in the Company's equity plan (for full-time team members). Remote social activities, including virtual coffee buddies. Bonusly - We use Bonusly as a way to recognize and reward team members for their hard work and commitment. This role is ideal for a results-driven marketing professional with a strong technical background and a keen eye for detail. If you are passionate about digital marketing and investor communications, we encourage you to apply and join a dynamic and innovative team. If we just described you and your perfect role, we'd love to talk with you. We have a lot to accomplish this year and look forward to making headway and creating success together! review_candidates.description: IT First Responder is a Managed IT and Cybersecurity provider supporting businesses across Australia. We’re looking for a Junior IT Support Technician to join our team in Castle Hill. This is a Level 1 support role suited to someone starting or building their career in IT. You may already have experience working in IT support, or you might currently be studying IT, Networking, Cyber Security or a related field at TAFE or equivalent and looking for an opportunity to turn what you’re learning into real-world experience. Working in an MSP means every day is different. You’ll work across multiple client environments and gain hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Windows, networking, cybersecurity and business technology. We don’t expect you to know everything. We do expect you to be curious, resourceful, genuinely interested in technology and willing to think through a problem. Before You Apply – Minimum Requirements Please only apply if the following requirements work for you. These are non-negotiable for this role. • This is NOT a remote role. The position is office-based in Castle Hill, NSW. Please consider your commute before applying. • Start time is 8:30 AM. Reliability and punctuality are essential. • You must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. This is a mandatory requirement for the position. • A valid Australian driver’s licence is required. • You should have some familiarity with Microsoft 365 and Windows environments. We don’t expect a junior technician to know every admin function, but you should be comfortable with technology and able to learn new systems. • Excellent spoken and written English is required. You’ll communicate directly with clients and document your work, so clear communication matters. • This is an MSP environment. You’ll support multiple businesses across different industries, each with different systems, setups and users. • You need to be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities and dealing professionally with frustrated users while setting clear expectations. What You’ll Be Doing • Providing remote and occasional onsite IT support to business clients • Troubleshooting Windows desktops and laptops • Supporting Microsoft 365 including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive • Assisting with user onboarding, offboarding, licensing and permissions in Microsoft 365 and Entra ID • Troubleshooting common network connectivity issues including Wi-Fi, DNS, DHCP and VPNs • Setting up and configuring computers, devices and peripherals • Supporting printers and common business applications • Monitoring and responding to alerts from RMM and monitoring systems • Maintaining clear and accurate ticket notes and technical documentation • Researching and troubleshooting technical issues you haven’t encountered before • Escalating more complex issues to senior technicians when appropriate, with clear notes on what you’ve already investigated and tried What We’re Looking For You do not need years of commercial IT experience to apply. We’re interested in candidates who either have previous IT support/helpdesk experience or are currently studying IT, Networking, Cyber Security or a related field at TAFE or equivalent. More importantly, we want someone with a genuine interest in technology. You should enjoy figuring things out. If you encounter something you haven’t seen before, your first instinct should be to investigate, research and understand the problem rather than immediately hand it to someone else. You’ll need: • A genuine interest in technology and how things work • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills • Curiosity and a willingness to learn • The ability to research problems you haven’t encountered before • Logical thinking and the ability to work through problems methodically • Good attention to detail • Strong communication and customer service skills • The ability to manage and prioritise multiple support requests • A calm and professional approach when dealing with client issues • The ability to use AI tools effectively and responsibly, while applying your own judgement rather than blindly following AI-generated instructions • The confidence to ask for help when you need it, while making a reasonable attempt to investigate the problem first Why Join IT First Responder? You’ll get exposure to far more than password resets. Working in an MSP gives you the opportunity to see different businesses, technologies and problems every day. You’ll build practical skills across Microsoft 365, networking, endpoint management, cybersecurity and cloud technologies while working alongside experienced technicians. For someone at the beginning of their IT career who actually likes technology and wants to learn, there’s a lot of opportunity to grow. How to Apply You can apply here or email olga@itfr.com.au (preferred). Please include the phrase “Attention to detail” in the subject line and briefly answer the following three questions: 1. A user reports that Outlook is not receiving emails. What is the first thing you would check? 2. A user says their computer will not turn on. What are the first two things you would check? 3. You’re troubleshooting an issue and ask an AI tool for assistance. It suggests three possible solutions: A. Check the relevant Windows Event Logs for errors relating to the issue. B. Verify the affected service is running and restart it if appropriate. C. Temporarily disable the endpoint security/EDR agent because it may be interfering with the application. How would you approach these suggestions, and what would you do next? We’re not looking for essay-length answers or perfectly worded technical responses. We want to understand how you think, troubleshoot and approach a problem. Applications that do not follow the application instructions may not be considered.

review_candidates.title: Application Support / Technical Support Engineer (Customer Engagement Specialist)
review_candidates.description: Application Support / Technical Support Engineer (Customer Engagement Specialist) , Enterprise LMS Location: Chenai Experience: 8 to 12 years Function: Product and Customer Engagement About the role This is not a ticket-routing job. PeopleOne earlier known as ExpertusONE is an enterprise learning platform used by global organisations to run compliance training, certification programs, instructor-led and virtual sessions, and skills development at scale across tens of thousands of learners. When something behaves unexpectedly in an environment like that, the question is rarely "did the user click the wrong button." It is usually a configuration interaction, an integration payload, a permissions model edge case, or a genuine defect hiding behind three layers of plausible explanations. We are looking for someone who can tell the difference, and prove it. You will own customer-reported issues end to end: reproduce them, isolate the root cause, resolve what can be resolved through configuration or guidance, and hand the rest to Engineering with a diagnosis sharp enough that they can start fixing instead of start investigating. You are the person who makes the difference between a bug report that says "enrollment is broken for this customer" and one that says "enrollment fails when a training plan has sequencing enforced and the learner holds a prior exempted module, here is the reproduction path, here are the three affected tenants, here is the query that identifies them." If you enjoy the puzzle more than the ticket count, read on. What you will do Investigate and diagnose Take ownership of escalated customer issues across the platform: enrollments, training plans, compliance and certification workflows, ILT and virtual classroom sessions, content playback (SCORM, xAPI, AICC, cmi5), reporting and analytics, notifications, mobile, and integrations. Reproduce issues in test environments. Establish what is configuration, what is data, what is expected behaviour that the customer did not expect, and what is a genuine defect. Query production data (read-only) to quantify blast radius: how many learners, which tenants, since when, and under what conditions. Read application and integration logs, trace API request and response payloads, and inspect webhook and SSO flows to isolate where a transaction actually failed. Distinguish correlation from causation. The most recent change is not automatically the cause. Resolve and communicate Resolve issues directly where the fix is configuration, data correction, workflow redesign, or customer enablement. Write customer-facing responses that a non-technical LMS administrator can act on: what happened, what the impact is, what we are doing, what they need to do, and by when. Manage expectations honestly on issues that will not be fixed quickly. Vague reassurance is worse than an inconvenient timeline. Run live troubleshooting sessions with customer administrators and IT teams including screen shares with enterprise security and identity teams. Escalate with a prognosis, not a summary Package defects for Engineering with a reproduction path, environment details, affected versions and tenants, log evidence, expected versus actual behaviour, and a stated hypothesis on root cause. Assign severity and business impact yourself, and defend that assessment. Everything is not a P1. Stay attached to the issue through to resolution. Escalation is a handoff of ownership for the fix, not a handoff of ownership for the customer. Improve the system Identify recurring issue patterns and drive them to permanent elimination: product change, documentation gap, onboarding defect, or default configuration problem. Build and maintain internal diagnostic runbooks and customer-facing knowledge articles. Reduce the number of issues that need you at all. Feed themes and evidence back into the product roadmap. You will have a direct line to Product Management and your input is expected to be substantiated with data, not anecdote. What success looks like By 90 days: You are independently resolving escalated issues across at least three functional areas without shadowing. Your defect reports are accepted by Engineering without a round trip for missing information. By six months: Your average escalated-to-Engineering rate is falling because you are resolving more at source. You have shipped knowledge articles or runbooks that measurably reduce repeat issues. You have raised at least two product changes that were accepted onto the roadmap. By twelve months: You are the person other engineers and CSMs come to when an issue does not make sense. You are trusted to speak directly to enterprise customers during severity incident without supervision. What you need Non-negotiable: 8 to 12 years in technical support, application support, product support engineering, or solutions engineering for a B2B SaaS or enterprise software product. Consumer support and pure L1 experience will not transfer. Working SQL. You must be able to write joins, aggregations, and filtered queries against a relational schema to investigate an issue yourself, without asking an engineer. Practical fluency with R EST APIs : reading documentation, constructing requests, interpreting status codes and error payloads, and using Postman or an equivalent tool. Demonstrated ability to read application logs and trace a transaction across systems. Structured diagnostic reasoning. You form a hypothesis, test it, and discard it when the evidence disagrees. Written English strong enough for direct communication with enterprise customers in EMEA and North America. Comfort with ambiguity and with saying "I do not know yet, here is how I will find out." Strongly preferred: Prior experience with an LMS, LXP, HCM, or talent management platform (Cornerstone, Docebo, Absorb, SuccessFactors Learning, Workday Learning, Saba, or similar). Understanding of e-learning standards: SCORM 1.2 and 2004, xAPI, AICC, cmi5, and LRS concepts. Enterprise integration experience: SAML and OIDC single sign-on, SCIM provisioning, HRIS data feeds, webhooks, and file-based imports. Exposure to BI or reporting tools (Superset, Tableau, Power BI) and the ability to validate a reporting discrepancy against source data. Experience supporting multi-tenant SaaS, including the reasoning required to separate tenant-specific configuration issues from platform defects. BE, BTech, MCA, or equivalent technical education. We care more about what you can do than where you learned it. What we are not looking for To save everyone time: This role does not involve reading from a script or routing tickets to a queue. This is not a Customer Success Manager role. It is not primarily about renewals, QBRs, or adoption metrics, although you will work closely with the people who own those. If your last three years have been spent exclusively in a tier-one queue with a strict escalation-after-fifteen-minutes policy, this will be a difficult jump. If you are looking for a step towards a pure development role, be honest about that in the interview and we will tell you honestly whether this is the right path. How we evaluate Beyond conversation, we will put a real anonymised issue in front of you: a description, some log output, and a data extract. We will ask you to tell us what you think is happening and what you would check next. We are assessing how you reason, not whether you already know our product. Why this role is worth your time You will get read-only production access, direct access to Engineering, and a direct line into Product Management where your findings shape what gets built. You will work on genuinely complex enterprise problems for recognisable global customers. And you will be measured on whether problems stay solved, not on how many tickets you closed. If you're passionate about troubleshooting complex enterprise applications and delivering exceptional customer outcomes, we'd love to connect. 📩 Apply now or share your profile with us @swethav@peopleone.co
